Read-only audit of the user's MCP server configuration on Windows (do not modify anything). Find and report where MCP servers are configured and enumerate them.

Explore these locations:
1. C:\Users\JeremyWilliams\.claude.json — this is likely large. Find the "mcpServers" object(s) (there may be per-project and global scopes). List every MCP server name, its command/args (redact any secret values but note WHICH env var names carry secrets), and scope. Also note any "enabledMcpjsonServers"/"disabledMcpjsonServers" and per-project mcp config.
2. C:\Users\JeremyWilliams\.claude\mcp-scaffold.json — report the full prior server inventory.
3. Any C:\Users\JeremyWilliams\.mcp.json or C:\Users\JeremyWilliams\.claude\.mcp.json if present.
4. Check C:\Users\JeremyWilliams\.claude\plugins\ — list installed plugins/marketplaces (directory names under plugins/ and plugins/marketplaces/ and plugins/cache/) so I know which plugins contribute MCP servers and agents (e.g. ecc, ruflo-core, vercel, etc.).

I am auditing for DUPLICATE connectors — e.g. Gmail available via native MCP AND Composio AND Make; Linear native vs Make; multiple memory servers (mcp__memory knowledge-graph, ruflo memory, supermemory). Report a table of: capability/app → every server/route that provides it → note the duplication. Also flag any servers configured but likely unused, and any secrets stored in plaintext in config.

Report exact server names and config keys so they can be edited later. Do NOT edit anything.
